newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr hovers in narrow range vs yen by Tokyo noon.
newsitem.headline: Dlr hovers in narrow range vs yen by Tokyo noon.

text.p: 0300 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT
The dollar moved narrowly against the yen by midday in Tokyo on Monday, after edging down earlier on selling by Japanese exporters and interbank players.

Traders said the dollar was capped by exporter offers above 114 yen, but the market lacked fresh incentives to push it below 113.50 yen. The mark's weakness against the yen also indirectly worked to cap the dollar against the yen, they said.
The mark was quoted around 63.83/86 yen at 0320 GMT, compared with around 64.15 yen in late New York on Friday.
The dollar closed at 113.98/03 yen and 1.7768/78 marks in New York on Friday.

"I think the dollar is heading down versus the yen, but the market is lacking incentives for a downward probe. We may just have to wait until the release of trade data in Japan and the United States later this week," said a trader at a trust bank.
Japan's customs-cleared trade balance for June will be released on Thursday while U.S. international trade data for May is due on Friday.
Traders said they expected the dollar, the yen and the pound to gain further against the mark amid worries about a weak euro, although some profit-taking is expected in the near term.

"A lot of people are expecting the dollar to climb to 1.8 marks. We could see a mild dip in the near term due to profit-taking, but that should give people a chance to set up new longs," said a city bank trader.
Technical indicators suggest that the mark could head down towards 61.50 yen if support around 63.10/20 yen does not hold, a trader at a long-term credit bank said.
Weakness in several Asian currencies was providing psychological support to the Japanese currency, traders said.
"Weakness of the Thai baht and the Philippine peso is partly responsible for making people reluctant to sell the yen, due to possible safe-haven yen buying," said a trader at another trust bank.

Some market participants were cautious about selling the dollar ahead of Tuesday's news conference by senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, who is to take over the post of vice finance minister for international affairs after the cabinet's expected approval of his promotion on Tuesday.

In addition to Sakakibara, outgoing vice finance minister for international affairs Takatoshi Kato, incoming vice finance minister Takeshi Komura and outgoing vice finance minister Tadashi Ogawa are scheduled to hold a news briefing on Tuesday afternoon.
Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita's opening speech on Monday at the start of a two-day BOJ branch managers' meeting had little impact on the forex market, traders said.
Matsushita said Japan's economy is continuing on a gradual recovery trend supported by firm production and incomes, despite the lingering impact of a rise in the consumption tax.
"Matsushita didn't say anything new. The market's interest seems to be moving away from Japanese economic conditions and interest rates," said a city bank trader.
Some traders said, however, that they will still be cautious ahead of news briefings by BOJ branch managers in the afternoon.
Comments by BOJ Osaka branch manager Eichiro Kinoshita and other branch managers are scheduled for release at 0930 GMT.
-- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
